actions.title: Create the GitHub copy you own
actions.instruction: Open the Academy fork page, choose your GitHub account as the owner, keep the repository name arbiter-academy, and create the fork.
actions.rationale: Your fork gives every lesson a push destination that you control.

resources.label: View the official read-only Academy repository

actions.expected_result: GitHub opens a repository named arbiter-academy under your account and identifies it as a fork of arbiterForge/arbiter-academy.
actions.recovery: If GitHub shows the official repository or another owner, return to the fork page and choose your own account before continuing.
actions.evidence: The browser address contains your account name followed by arbiter-academy.

actions.title: Clone your fork
actions.instruction: Run the variant for your operating system in a Native terminal after replacing <your-account> with the owner of your fork.
actions.rationale: Cloning your fork makes origin point to a repository you own.
actions.expected_result: Git creates an arbiter-academy folder and reports that the clone completed.
actions.recovery: If GitHub asks for access or Git says the repository was not found, confirm the account name and that the fork exists before retrying.
actions.evidence: The new clone records your fork as origin.

actions.title: Enter the cloned repository
actions.instruction: Run the variant for your operating system in the same Native terminal that created the clone.
actions.rationale: Every later command must target the practice repository rather than its parent folder.
actions.expected_result: The Native terminal prompt is inside the cloned arbiter-academy repository.
actions.recovery: If the folder is not found, list the current folder and confirm where Git created arbiter-academy before trying again.
actions.evidence: The terminal's current directory ends with arbiter-academy.

actions.title: Install the reviewed Academy tools
actions.instruction: Run only the fast installer for your operating system in a Native terminal whose current directory is the clone.
actions.rationale: The piped script validates the downloaded bundle against its reviewed digest. It does not verify its own already-executing bytes. Use the linked source and checksum when you need to verify the installer before execution.

resources.label: Review the immutable PowerShell installer source
Review the immutable POSIX installer source

actions.expected_result: The installer reports Preview 0.5 and the path of the installed arbiter-academy executable.
actions.recovery: If verification or installation stops, preserve the complete message and use the linked source plus checksum before deciding whether to retry.
actions.evidence: The installed tool lives outside the learner repository at the versioned Preview 0.5 path.

actions.title: Record the first readiness baseline
actions.instruction: Run the installed Academy Doctor command from the clone, read every reported boundary, and continue to F01 when any failures are limited to the expected fresh-clone remote findings.
actions.rationale: Doctor records a baseline; F01 owns the first lesson's remote repair and readiness proof.

resources.label: Ask a course question in Academy Discussions

actions.expected_result: Doctor reports Python and Git versions, the repository root, worktree and branch state, remotes and effective push routing, upstream push protection, and codeArbiter activation and initialization without changing the repository.
actions.recovery: If Doctor reports only missing upstream or related fresh-clone remote evidence, continue to F01. If origin is not your fork, main is dirty, or another prerequisite is unavailable, stop and correct only that setup boundary before Prepare.
actions.evidence: The Doctor report is a baseline. A later passing report is readiness evidence, not lesson completion evidence.
